evidence.ref: Current setup/login is a single app_state admin_password hash and signs every session in as name=admin without a role claim (Security.cs, Program.cs).
All existing /api routes are authentication-only and inherit CSRF validation; this enables a group/policy authorization retrofit without changing endpoint business behavior (Program.cs).
StateStore initializes SQLite only with app_state and can safely create additive tables using CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS in InitializeAsync (StateStore.cs).
Persistence tests establish the current one-admin bootstrap contract and isolated SQLite test setup (PersistenceTests.cs).

Endpoint authorization matrix: unauthenticated=/health, /api/auth/status, POST /api/auth/setup only before configured, POST /api/auth/login; authenticated any role=POST /api/auth/logout, GET /api/auth/me, POST /api/auth/password; viewer+admin+owner=all existing read-only GET API routes plus /hubs/status; admin+owner=all existing state-changing server/settings/save/backup/version/mod/player endpoints; owner only=/api/users* and GET /api/audit-events. Preserve CSRF on every authenticated unsafe method, including account management.

next_slice.summary: Developer scope: add UserRole/domain request-response records, AccountService and AuditService, additive StateStore initialization/migration, role policies/helpers, cookie claim validation/sign-in changes, owner account/audit endpoints, authorization annotations for existing API groups, and focused persistence/integration tests. Migration is transactional: create tables/indexes; if users is empty and app_state.admin_password exists, insert fixed legacy username 'admin' as owner using the existing BCrypt hash and write a bootstrap audit event; then use users as the sole authentication authority. Retain the legacy hash only for rollback compatibility in this milestone, never consult it after users exists; do not log passwords, hashes, CSRF values, cookies, Factorio credentials, server passwords, request bodies, or player names. Audit successful and failed login, setup, password/account/role/delete operations, and successful/failed/denied privileged mutations. Details JSON is a small allowlisted, secret-free summary; audit failures must not convert a successful operational mutation into a failure, but should be logged and surfaced through application logging. Pagination is newest-first with owner-only GET /api/audit-events?beforeId=&limit= (bounded 1..100).

result: Implement RBAC with normalized SQLite tables while retaining app_state. Data model: users(id TEXT PK UUID, username TEXT NOT NULL COLLATE NOCASE UNIQUE, password_hash TEXT NOT NULL, role TEXT NOT NULL CHECK role IN ('owner','admin','viewer'), security_stamp TEXT NOT NULL, created_at_utc TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at_utc TEXT NOT NULL); audit_events(id INTEGER PK AUTOINCREMENT, occurred_at_utc TEXT NOT NULL, actor_user_id TEXT NULL, action TEXT NOT NULL, target_type TEXT NOT NULL, target_id TEXT NULL, outcome TEXT NOT NULL CHECK outcome IN ('success','failure','denied'), details_json TEXT NOT NULL). First setup creates the sole owner. Owner-only account endpoints: GET /api/users, POST /api/users (admin/viewer only), PATCH /api/users/{id}/role (admin/viewer only), POST /api/users/{id}/password, DELETE /api/users/{id}; reject deleting/demoting the owner and self-deletion. Any authenticated user may POST /api/auth/password for their own password. Cookie claims are uid, name, role, csrf, and security_stamp; validate uid/stamp against users on every request, rejecting disabled/deleted/changed accounts. Force legacy cookie invalidation by changing the cookie name/version during rollout.
